questions.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨9t-4,\,2{t}^{3}+5⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(9t-4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}+5)⟩ \\  & =⟨9,\,6{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨4{t}^{3},\,-2{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(1)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨12{t}^{2},\,-4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨12(1)^{2},\,-4(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨12,\,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨12,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨{2}^{t-1},\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{t-1}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{t-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨{2}^{1-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2(1)}{({1}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{0}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{2}{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{1}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡2,-\frac{1}{2}⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{ln}^{2}⁡2+\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{4{ln}^{2}⁡2+1}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{4{ln}^{2}⁡2+1}}{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\frac{\pi }{8}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=\frac{\pi }{8},$ we substitute $t=\frac{\pi }{8}$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}),2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨4\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},2\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨4,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(\frac{\pi }{8})|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(\frac{\pi }{8})| & =|⟨4,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+4} \\  & =\sqrt{20} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{5}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+6t-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨5{t}^{4}-2t,\,2t+6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{4}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+6)⟩ \\  & =⟨20{t}^{3}-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =⟨20(0)^{3}-2,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
